name: Semantic model tests: known input, known output

why.matters: Measures are code. A small table whose answers you can work out by hand turns "the total looks plausible" into a test that fails the moment a measure changes behaviour.
why.failure: Someone "fixes" time intelligence and YoY silently changes for every month that crosses a year boundary; nobody notices until the annual review.
why.use: A mini dataset with hand-computed answers, DAX queries (EVALUATE) that return measure values in specific filter contexts, and a stored expected result to compare against after every change.
why.avoid: Testing only on production data, where you don't know the right answer.

verified.context: DAX query view (Power BI Desktop, Sept 2026)

asg.t: Work the answers out by hand first
steps: Open mini_sales.csv: eight lines. Value = Qty × UnitPrice. L8 is a return (negative quantity).
On paper, compute: total sales; Q1 2025; Q1 2026 by order date; Q1 2026 by ship date; YoY for Q1; distinct customers in 2026 and in March 2026; Online sales in Q1 2026.
Load the file into a new Power BI file with a date table: an active relationship on OrderDate, an inactive one on ShipDate.
Write the measures: Sales, Sales (ship date) with USERELATIONSHIP, Sales PY, YoY %, Customers.
Compare every measure with your paper answers.
asg.exp: Total {{qa_total|int}}; Q1 2025 {{qa_q1_2025|int}}; Q1 2026 {{qa_q1_2026|int}} by order date and {{qa_q1_2026_ship|int}} by ship date; YoY {{qa_yoy|pct1}}; {{qa_customers_2026|int}} customers in 2026, {{qa_customers_mar_2026|int}} in March 2026; Online Q1 2026 {{qa_online_q1_2026|int}}.

asg.t: Turn them into a DAX test query
asg.brief: Write one DAX query that returns each test's name, expected value, actual value and pass/fail, so anyone can rerun the whole suite in seconds after a change.
req: One row per test, including the inactive-relationship and year-boundary cases.
Expected values typed in from your paper answers, not copied from the measures.
A pass flag that tolerates rounding.
asg.exp: Every row shows Pass. Change Sales PY to use DATEADD(…, -12, MONTH) incorrectly on purpose and at least the YoY test fails.

asg.t: What should a measure return here?
asg.brief: Total rows and edge cases are where measures break. Decide what each measure should return in four awkward contexts, test it, and fix what's wrong.
req: YoY % for a month with no sales last year.
Customers at the grand total (is it the sum of the months?).
Sales for a product filtered to a date range with only a return.
Sales (ship date) for March 2026, when one March order ships in April.
asg.exp: YoY blank (not infinity or 0) without prior-year sales; customers at the total = distinct across the period, not the sum of months; the return-only context shows a negative number; ship-date March excludes the line shipped in April.

int.q: What is a known-input, known-output test for a measure?
int.a: A small dataset where you've worked out the correct results by hand, and a query that evaluates the measure in specific filter contexts and compares with those results. If the measure or the model changes behaviour, the test fails.

int.q: Which contexts most often break measures?
int.a: Totals (non-additive measures), year and period boundaries (time intelligence), blank or missing data (division, YoY), negative values (returns), inactive relationships and many-to-many paths.

int.q: How do you run model tests automatically?
int.a: Store the test queries (DAX) and expected results in the repository; run them with DAX query view by hand, or automatically through the XMLA endpoint or the executeQueries REST API after deployment, and fail the pipeline on mismatches.

int.q: Why type expected values in instead of computing them with another measure?
int.a: Computing them with DAX can reproduce the same mistake. Independent expected values (by hand, SQL or Excel) are what make it a test.

ass.q: Your DAX test says YoY for January 2026 = blank. January 2025 had no sales. Is that right?
o: Yes: there is no prior value to compare with
ass.why: DIVIDE returns blank when the denominator is blank or zero, which is the honest answer.

ass.q: The distinct customer count for Q1 is lower than the sum of the three months. This means:
o: Some customers bought in more than one month

ass.q: Store your DAX test query and its expected output in the repository next to the PBIP, and write a one-paragraph README on how to run it.
ass.hint: Later, the automation track shows how to run it against the Service with the executeQueries REST API.
